name: Tute americano
description: Tute americano: Tute variant with American deck (52 cards) or 40-card strip. Same point-trick and Cantes logic; variant rules.

overview.description: Tute americano: Tute variant with American deck (52 cards) or 40-card strip. Same point-trick and Cantes logic; variant rules.

history.origins: Tute originated in Italy as tutti and spread to Spain in the 19th century, becoming one of the most popular card games there and in Latin America. Tute americano is a two-player variant that follows the same point-trick and marriage (cantes) logic as Tute corriente but is played with a 40- or 52-card deck and differs in hand size (eight cards), no tute declaration, and a 121-point target.
timeline: Traditional: Tute family documented in Spain and Latin America; americano variant played with 40- or 52-card deck.

setup.players: Two players only; no partnerships. Non-dealer leads first; turn to deal alternates.
setup.dealing: Eight cards each, one at a time; turn one face up for trump; rest form stock.

rules.objective: First to 121 or more points from tricks, last trick (10), and singing (20/40). No tute (four kings or horses) declaration.
rules.gameplay: Same as Tute corriente except: eight cards each; turn one for trump, rest to stock. Non-dealer leads. While stock has cards: if trump is led you must play a trump (need not overtake); if non-trump led you may play any card. When stock is exhausted: follow suit, beat led card if possible, trump if void. After winning a trick you may sing one 40 or 20 (king-horse of same suit). Winner of trick draws first from stock, then opponent. First to 121+ wins.
keyRules: Trump lead must play trump in first part

scoring.winCondition: First to 121 or more points from card points in tricks, last trick (10), and cantes (20/40).
